title: Cucumber Pomegranate Salad With Mint
description: By Naz Deravian: Cucumber pomegranate salad is an early fall love story that confidently leaps into winter. Crisp and sweet Persian cucumbers are a welcome companion to ruby-red, tart pomegranate seeds, the jewels of cooler months. Tossed with red onion and both dried and fresh mint, this colorful and tangy salad enlivens a meal and your taste buds. There’s no need to prepare the dressing separately; drizzle and sprinkle everything directly on. The juice from the pomegranate seeds mingling with the lime juice makes for a pink-hued dressing that is worthy of slurping directly from a spoon.
ingredients: 3 Persian cucumbers, quartered lengthwise and sliced into ¼-inch pieces
½ medium red onion, finely chopped into ¼-inch pieces
Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and black pepper
2 tablespoons lime juice, plus more to taste (from 2 medium limes)
Large handful of fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped
directions: Place the chopped onions in some water or vinegar for a few minutes, if you’d like to soften their onion bite or add a little vinegar sparkle.
Place the cucumbers, red onion and pomegranate seeds in a medium bowl.
Drizzle with the olive oil; sprinkle salt (about ½ teaspoon) and pepper to taste.
Add 2 tablespoons lime juice, dried mint and fresh mint. Stir and taste.
Add more lime juice as needed. It should make your lips smack with its tang, in a good way. Adjust for salt and serve.
Optionally, add a little crumbled or cubed Feta to round out the flavors.
